root_cause.text: In the error path of octep_vf_request_irqs(), the rollback loop uses the wrong device ID ('oct') when calling free_irq(), instead of the same ioq_vector that was used in request_irq(), causing the IRQ to remain registered and leading to use-after-free when ioq_vector is later freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `free_irq(oct->msix_entries[i].vector, oct)` to `free_irq(oct->msix_entries[i].vector, oct->ioq_vector[i])`. The CVE description explicitly states the mismatch: "requests MSI-X queue IRQs with dev_id set to ioq_vector. ... rollback loop calls free_irq() with dev_id set to 'oct'", and the consequence: "This can keep IRQ handlers alive while ioq_vector is later freed ... leading to a use-after-free or crash when an interrupt fires."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix IRQ cleanup in octep_vf to use the correct per-queue dev_id when freeing IRQs on error.
intent_record.what: Changed the second argument of free_irq() in the error cleanup loop from oct to oct->ioq_vector[i].
intent_record.how: This ensures that when freeing IRQs during error handling, the correct per-queue cookie (dev_id) is used, matching the one used during request_irq. Using the wrong dev_id could cause incorrect cleanup behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Fix IRQ cleanup in octep_vf to use the correct per-queue dev_id when freeing IRQs on error.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address the vulnerability root cause by fixing the IRQ cleanup in octep_vf_request_irqs() to use the correct per-queue dev_id when freeing IRQs, preventing use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This statement passes 'oct' as the dev_id to free_irq, but the corresponding request_irq used the per-queue ioq_vector. This mismatch causes free_irq to fail to deregister the IRQ handler, leaving the IRQ registered and leading to use-after-free when ioq_vector is later freed.
